q2_zoningUnmeasured.isThisMorningsFixWorkingCorrectly: Yes, established, not assumed. Before today's classifyRequiredLeaf change (verify-walk.mjs:254-284, P-124 CTX-LEAVES 2026-09-08), any object with an unrecognised verdict token fell through to an unconditional {state:'value', ok:true} -- so a served zoning object carrying verdict:'unmeasured' would have PASSED the walk as populated. The walk refusing it now is strictly more correct, not a regression: it surfaces a real, pre-existing, architecture-level vocabulary mismatch (doc-19 Section Layer's 5-state LayerAbsenceVerdict vs. the four-state leaf contract) that was previously invisible to grading. _decisions/2026-09-01_serve_path_never_emits_pipeline_state.md already ruled this exact shape of leak (citing cityLimitsFact.status and etjStatus, both siblings of zoning.verdict in the same object) must convert at the serve boundary to absent-verified-with-basis or refused, and explicitly rejected adding a fifth completeness state -- but that ruling was never implemented against verdictLayerServe.ts's zoning path, which still stands unmodified on origin/main with unmeasured as one of 5 deliberate, tested verdicts.
q2_zoningUnmeasured.whyNotAbsentVerified: absent-verified in this program's vocabulary means a POSITIVE, confirmed absence (AGENT_CONTRACT Section 5: 'an empty result is NOT an absence'). 'unmeasured' here means the opposite -- containment could not be determined either way (no parcel_record row to read, or an undeclared county doctrine). Collapsing it to absent-verified would misrepresent an unresolved lookup as a verified absence. The decision's own text offers refused as the other valid conversion target, which does not claim a determination was made -- that is the honest fit, not absent-verified.
